assets.statement: Parity lemma refuted by Kummer: k&(n−k)=0 gives odd C(n,k); (7,3)=35 with lpf 5>7/2, and infinitely many (2^m−1,k) instances; branch-A close must instead bound small prime factors of odd coefficients directly.

REFUTED by external audit (GPT gold-mine audit + R4, 2026-09-01), each item re-verified by the operator's session against the frozen contract or by exact computation on 2026-09-02 | FALSE: Pintz/Rankin-type results concern LARGE GAPS between consecutive primes, not the length of arithmetic progressions of primes in [1,N]. No theorem gives L(N) = omega(log N) infinitely often; the longest known prime APs in [1,N] have length far below log N and the o(log N) question is open. 'negative close achieved' is a citation misuse.

Finite-A periodic proof is domain drift: canonical ∀A⊆ℕ includes infinite A where periodicity/tail control vanishes; repair requires an analytic reduction (e.g. tail bounds uniform over all n∈A, m>x) or an explicit infinite-A counterexample with literal negation of the limit — neither exists on reco

refuted at smallest parameters: r=2, k=2 family I₁={2,3}, I₂={24,25} gives total product 3600=60², exactly verified; Pell a(a+1)=6t² yields infinitely many length-2 square-product blocks, so k=2 imposes no obstruction and any close must use a fixed r across all k≥2 with explicit integrality.
Counterexample r=36 (p=151, p_{r+1}=157, g=6): all five interior integers 152–156 have a prime factor ≥6; ∀-over-gaps form must be weakened to a selected-subsequence construction.

the 43-row certificate is false: direct enumeration of pairs (a,b)≠(0,0) with 2^a·3^b ≤ 1000 gives 39 rows (b=0:9, b=1:9, b=2:7, b=3:6, b=4:4, b=5:3, b=6:1); also (0,1)↦3−1=2 is a prime row, the only empty-factorization row is (1,0)↦1; repair is a 39-row table, and Set.Infinite transfer remains bloc
